summary: Rewrote src/index.ts from a single-purpose server launcher into a CLI command dispatcher.
Parses process.argv[2] (defaulting to 'menu') and routes to: showMenu(), startServerCommand(), runSetup(), generateDocs(), or printUsage() + exit(1) for unknown commands.

startServerCommand() wraps existing server-start logic: loadConfig() in try/catch with helpful error + 'Run paralizer setup' suggestion on failure, --verbose flag support, staticDir resolved via getToolRoot() instead of __dirname-relative path.
printUsage() outputs a clean help message listing all four commands and the --verbose option.
Used an async IIFE for top-level async dispatch (CJS-compatible).
Removed the old __dirname-based staticDir in favour of path.resolve(getToolRoot(), 'gui', 'public') — consistent with how menu.ts resolves it.
Build: tsc exits 0. All 539 tests pass.

comments.note: src/index.ts: The previous code used path.resolve(__dirname, '..', 'gui', 'public') to locate the static directory. This was brittle — __dirname points to dist/ so the '../' hop was an implicit implementation detail. The new code uses getToolRoot() (same as menu.ts), which is more explicit and consistent. No action needed; noted for context.

src/utils/paths.ts: Uses 'node:fs' and 'node:path' without the 'node:' protocol prefix (import * as fs from 'fs'). All other modules in src/ use the 'node:' prefix consistently (e.g. src/cli/docs.ts, src/cli/menu.ts). Minor inconsistency; consider updating to 'node:fs' and 'node:path' in a cleanup pass.

src/index.ts: The async IIFE pattern ((async () => { ... })()) is the correct approach for top-level async dispatch in CJS. If this project ever migrates to ESM, it can be replaced with a direct top-level await. Not a current concern but worth flagging for a future ESM migration.

comments.note: src/index.ts has no dedicated unit test file. The entry-point dispatch logic (command routing, printUsage, startServerCommand error path) is only validated by live runtime invocation and code inspection. Given the simplicity of the logic (switch + process.exit), the risk is low, but adding a tests/index.test.ts with process.argv mocking + spies on showMenu/runSetup/generateDocs would improve regression coverage.

Live test confirmed that 'paralizer --help' falls through to the default branch (printUsage + exit 1), which is intentional and correct per spec. No --help special-case is needed given the existing design.

The async IIFE's unhandled rejection path (if any of the dispatched commands throw unexpectedly) is not caught at the top level. Node.js will emit an UnhandledPromiseRejection warning but not crash with a clean error message. A .catch(err => { process.stderr.write(...); process.exit(1); }) on the IIFE would make unexpected failures more user-friendly. Low priority — all current callees handle their own errors.

summary: Code review PASS for WP-004 — Binary Entry Point Update (src/index.ts).

Structure & readability: The rewrite is clean and minimal. The JSDoc header comment precisely documents every command and the --verbose option. The async IIFE + switch pattern is idiomatic and easy to follow. Section dividers (// --- Private helpers ---) match the existing style used across the codebase.

Correctness: Command dispatch logic matches the spec exactly. Default to 'menu' via nullish coalescing is correct. The 'serve' path guards loadConfig() inside a try/catch and calls process.exit(1) with two helpful stderr lines — no config-loading side-effects bleed into setup/docs/menu paths.

Error paths: startServerCommand() has a secondary try/catch wrapping startServer() itself, emitting a clean stderr message and exit(1) on server-start failure. This is a nice defensive layer beyond the spec's requirement.

Flag handling: process.argv.includes('--verbose') scanning full argv is correct — users could theoretically place --verbose anywhere. This is more permissive than only accepting it after 'serve', which is appropriate for a CLI tool.
Path resolution: staticDir via path.resolve(getToolRoot(), 'gui', 'public') is consistent with menu.ts and removes the __dirname hop fragility. Confirmed correct.

Imports: All imports in src/index.ts correctly use the 'node:path' protocol prefix. The pre-existing inconsistency in src/utils/paths.ts (bare 'fs'/'path' imports) was noted by the Developer and is out-of-scope for WP-004 — confirm as a pre-existing debt item.
printUsage(): Output matches the spec's prescribed help block verbatim. Printing to stdout (via console.log) is conventional for usage messages on unknown commands.
No regressions introduced: only src/index.ts was modified; the full 539-test suite passes.

comments.note: src/index.ts L102-105: The secondary try/catch around startServer() emits a generic 'repo-parallelizer error: <message>' to stderr and exits 1. This is correct but slightly inconsistent with the config-load error path at L73-75 which emits two lines (error + setup hint). If startServer() can fail for config-related reasons, the same hint would be helpful. Very low priority — startServer() failures are typically network/port errors, not config errors.

src/utils/paths.ts (pre-existing, out-of-scope for WP-004): bare 'fs' and 'path' imports vs. 'node:fs' and 'node:path' used everywhere else. Flagged as a cleanup item for a future housekeeping pass — no action required in this WP.

The async IIFE has no top-level .catch(). QA flagged this too. With all current callees handling their own errors it is safe, but adding .catch(err => { process.stderr.write(`repo-parallelizer: unexpected error: ${err.message}\n`); process.exit(1); }) would harden against future regressions. Low-priority cleanup candidate.
